newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Differences remain after NATO-Russia talks.
newsitem.headline: Differences remain after NATO-Russia talks.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana had five hours of talks on Monday but said they failed to resolve differences over the Western alliance's expansion plans.
The two sides released almost identical statements after the meeting, which also discussed creating a special relatonship between Russia and NATO.
They said they had agreed a schedule for more talks but warned that they would not be easy.
"The meeting was useful although, of course, there are different approaches on a range of questions," a brief Russian foreign ministry statement said.
"Discussions will be continued. A timetable has been set for future work. It is clear that it will not be easy but the two sides will try to make them a success."
The wording of the NATO statement, issued by alliance headquarters in Brussels, was almost the same. It said "different approaches exist on a range of issues".
Solana left Moscow after a 24-hour visit without talking to reporters. Primakov also declined to meet the media.

Russia opposes NATO's plans to take in new members from eastern and central Europe, saying this would threaten its security and create new divisions in Europe. Solana had hoped to ease Moscow's fears during his visit.
